title: Family Rhythm Pack
description: Short routines for the whole family together. They add a little predictability and a few shared moments to the week, for any age.

routines.title: Lay Out Tomorrow
routines.description: Five minutes in the evening to set out bags, clothes and anything needed for the morning.
routines.parentGoal: Move decisions out of the morning rush.
routines.childOutcome: Calmer mornings with fewer last-minute searches and arguments.
steps: Pick a regular time after dinner and say, 'Let's get tomorrow ready.'
Everyone sets out their own bag, clothes and anything they'll need.
Do yours at the same time, then check off together: 'Bags, clothes, done.'

routines.title: High and Low at Dinner
routines.description: Everyone shares one high and one low from their day.
routines.parentGoal: Create a regular, low-pressure moment where feelings are shared and heard.
routines.childOutcome: Gets practice naming feelings and hears that hard moments are normal.
steps: At dinner, go first: share your high and your low in a sentence each.
Go around the table; anyone can pass.
Just listen and say 'thanks for sharing', without fixing or advice.

routines.title: Look at the Week Together
routines.description: A short weekend check-in on what's coming up for everyone.
routines.parentGoal: Make the week predictable so changes aren't a surprise.
routines.childOutcome: Knows what's coming, which makes transitions and busy days easier.
steps: Sit together for five minutes on the weekend.
Go through the days: school, activities, anything different from usual.
Ask each person: 'Is there anything you're looking forward to or worried about?'

routines.title: Ten-Minute Reset
routines.description: Everyone tidies together for one song or a short timer, then stops.
routines.parentGoal: Share household tasks in a way that feels light and finite.
routines.childOutcome: Helps out without a battle because it's short, shared and has a clear end.
steps: Put on a song or set a ten-minute timer.
Everyone picks one area or one kind of thing to put away.
Stop when the music stops, even if it's not finished, and notice what got done.

routines.title: Screens Down Together
routines.description: A short, regular moment when everyone puts their screens away at the same time, parents included.
routines.parentGoal: Make screen limits shared rather than a rule only for the children.
routines.childOutcome: Accepts the break more easily when the adults do it too, and gets unhurried time together.
steps: Agree on a regular time and a place where devices go.
Put yours there first and say, 'Phones are having a rest.'
Do something simple together: a card game, a walk, or just talking.
